definition: Twilight is sunlight scattered through the atmosphere while the Sun is below the horizon.
label: What is twilight?

definition: Orbital motion is movement around another object under the pull of gravity.
label: How does an orbit work?

definition: The daytime Moon is the Moon seen during daylight, when it is above the horizon and bright enough to see.
label: Can the moon be up in the daytime?

definition: Moon phases are the changing views of the Moon’s sunlit half as it orbits Earth.
label: Why does the Moon change shape?

definition: Tides are changes in sea level driven mainly by the Moon’s and Sun’s gravity, with local patterns shaped by coastlines and the ocean floor.
label: What causes tides?

definition: A synodic month is one complete cycle of Moon phases, lasting about 29.5 days.
label: What is a synodic month?

definition: Tidal locking is rotation that takes the same time as one orbit, keeping the same side facing the object being orbited.
label: What is tidal locking?

definition: Libration is the Moon’s apparent rocking as seen from Earth, which lets us see a little beyond its usual edges over time.
label: What is libration?

definition: Moonrise delay is the change in the Moon’s rising time from one day to the next; it usually rises later as it moves along its orbit.
label: Why does moonrise get later each night?

definition: The Moon’s orbital tilt is the angle of about 5° between its orbit around Earth and Earth’s orbit around the Sun.
label: Why isn’t there an eclipse every month?

definition: The asteroid belt is a region between Mars and Jupiter containing many small bodies orbiting the Sun, including the dwarf planet Ceres.
label: What is the asteroid belt?

definition: Mars’s reddish color comes mainly from iron oxides in dust on its surface.
label: Why is Mars red?

definition: Triton’s retrograde orbit carries it around Neptune in the opposite direction to Neptune’s rotation.
label: Why does Triton orbit Neptune backwards?

definition: Saturn’s moons are natural objects that orbit Saturn, ranging from large worlds such as Titan to small icy and rocky bodies.
label: Why does Saturn have so many moons?

definition: Moon formation is the process by which natural satellites develop, including formation around a planet, impacts and capture.
label: Why do planets have moons, and how are they made?

definition: Planet formation is the growth of planets from material in a disk around a young star.
label: How were the planets formed?

definition: A dwarf planet orbits the Sun, is nearly round under its own gravity, has not cleared its orbital neighborhood, and is not a moon.
label: Why is Pluto a dwarf planet and not a planet?

definition: Daylight saving time is a seasonal change to local clocks, usually one hour ahead of standard time during part of the year.
label: What is daylight saving time?

definition: A leap year has an extra day to help keep the calendar aligned with Earth’s orbit; in the Gregorian calendar, that day is February 29.
label: What is a leap year?

definition: The International Date Line is an imaginary boundary across the Pacific where the calendar date changes by one day.
label: What is the International Date Line?

definition: Military time is a way of writing 24-hour time using four digits, such as 1430 for 2:30 PM.
label: How do you calculate military time?

definition: A solstice is an instant when the Sun reaches its farthest position north or south of the celestial equator during the year.
label: What is a solstice?

definition: An equinox is an instant when the Sun crosses the celestial equator, occurring once in March and once in September.
label: What is an equinox?

definition: A supermoon is a new or full Moon near its closest point to Earth; the term is most often used for a full Moon.
label: What is a supermoon?

definition: A blue moon commonly means the second full Moon in a calendar month; another definition is the third full Moon in a season containing four.
label: What is a blue moon?

definition: Moon phase names describe eight stages of the cycle: new, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full, waning gibbous, last quarter and waning crescent.
label: What are the moon phases called?

definition: The far side of the Moon is the hemisphere that mostly faces away from Earth; it receives sunlight too.
label: Does the Moon have a dark side?

definition: Spring tides have a larger tidal range near new and full Moon; neap tides have a smaller range near first and last quarter.
label: What is a spring tide?
